decisions.reason: Broadening the permitted source collection does not change the requirement to select substantive moments with a lesson, story, or real point.
The source decision changes which YouTube videos may be used, not the requirement that each resulting clip be complete and independently understandable.
Permitting any YouTube video does not alter the current 70-to-85-second clip duration.
The broader source collection does not modify the requirement to follow the current hook guidelines.
Source-video choice does not change the requirements for mood-appropriate music or its volume relative to the speaker.
The message permits a broader set of YouTube source videos but does not direct any change to the dedicated account's provisioning, branding, profile, or audience-routing configuration.
Changing the permitted video source does not change the clean, simple visual-editing standard or its prohibited treatments.
The source decision expands content selection but does not alter the assigned count of 12 clips or the obligation to create and submit the launch batch.
Allowing any YouTube source video does not alter the rule that B-roll must naturally support and strengthen the selected message.
The broadened source selection does not remove or modify the requirement for client approval before publication.
The permitted source collection has no effect on the white-text-only and no-text-effects caption standard.
The source-selection change does not alter the monthly target, approval basis, approval authority, or treatment of rejected clips.
